content.statement: An enterprise engaged in a hazardous or inherently dangerous activity owes an absolute and non-delegable duty to the community; harm from that activity attracts liability without the exceptions recognised under Rylands v. Fletcher.
content.development: Articulated in M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (Oleum Gas Leak) by Justice P.N. Bhagwati as an Indian response to industrial risk.
content.application: Use for hazardous industrial escapes and community harm; do not reduce to ordinary negligence without analysis.
exceptions: Not a general substitute for all negligence claims
Still requires the hazardous-enterprise factual predicate
